newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police receive Dassault bribe probe papers.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police receive Dassault bribe probe papers.

text.p: A French court has handed Belgian police papers relating to allegations French aerospace group Dassault paid bribes to win a military contract, RTBF radio reported on Tuesday.

The radio said it took high level contacts between Belgian Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck and French Justice Minister Jacques Toubon to secure the court's cooperation, more than a year after the information was requested.
"I intervened to the extent that communication was necessary," De Clerck told RTBF.

Belgian police are investigating claims Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($19 million) in kickbacks to Belgian political parties to secure a 1989 contract to fit air defence systems to the countries' F-16 fighter jets.

A Belgian court last year issued an international arrest warrant for Serge Dassault, group founder and chairman, who has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions relating to the affair.

Dassault was questioned by a French court, in the presence of Belgian investigators, in Paris in November 1995. A Paris property said to be related to a front company used to pay the bribes was also raided at that time.

La Libre Belgique newspaper reported separately on Tuesday that Belgian investigators were unhappy with the way the French court had transcribed Dassault's interview and believed they had not been given all relevant papers.
"Now the documents are there I am waiting for the conclusions of the inquiry. But it's not me who is doing this work," De Clerck told RTBF radio.
La Libre Belgique reported Belgian investigators would go to Paris a second time to continue their inquiries once the papers received by the French court have been analysed.
